newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa drifts higher on weaker sterling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa drifts higher on weaker sterling.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa drifted higher in quiet trading on Monday and traders said it was likely to continue edging upwards this week on the back of weaker sterling.
"Cocoa is very quiet. It's currency-bound at the moment. The market steadied a bit today on the back of weaker sterling, but it's got no direction at all," a trader said.
Active December, which accounted for more than half the volume, rose 19 stg to 1,050 while nearby March rose 16 stg to 1,070 and first month September also rose 19 stg to 1,021.
The back months rose by up to 10 stg.
Volume was 3,787 lots but traders said half of this was crosses and swaps. "Volume is very poor. Real volume today was probably about 1,800," a trader said.
Traders felt the market had the potential to move up but so few people were currently involved in it that this was not really being reflected in trading.
"I think it's going to do it very slowly. It will drift higher, maybe this week," he added.
